skill.name: gpt-image-edit
skill.description: Guides GPT Image 2 image edits through the RunComfy CLI, with prompt patterns for preservation, multilingual text changes, layout edits, and multi-reference composition.
skill.summary: Run GPT Image 2 edit workflows on RunComfy with preservation-focused prompt guidance.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The skill is Markdown-only, and most static backtick, URL, and traversal detections are documentation false positives. Real risks remain because the skill instructs use of the RunComfy CLI, sends prompts and image URLs to a third-party API, and stores an API token in a hidden config path.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before installing or running the RunComfy CLI, and show the exact command before execution.
Add a clear consent notice that prompts, image URLs, and outputs are processed by RunComfy services.

remediation.issue: Persisted API token in hidden config path
remediation.suggestion: Document the token file path, permissions, logout process, and manual removal steps for shared or ephemeral machines.

content.user_title: Edit Images with GPT Image 2 on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Precise image edits often drift, especially when text, layout, or identity must stay stable. This skill provides RunComfy GPT Image 2 edit workflows with preservation-focused prompts.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to invoke the RunComfy GPT Image 2 edit endpoint through the local CLI.
Documents the prompt, images, and size fields used by the edit endpoint.
Provides prompt patterns for preservation, multilingual text, spatial edits, and multi-reference composition.
Compares GPT Image Edit with Nano Banana Edit, Flux Kontext, and GPT Image 2 text-to-image.
Lists RunComfy CLI prerequisites, exit codes, troubleshooting links, and security notes.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and internet access.
Requires publicly fetchable HTTPS image URLs for model inputs.
Supports up to 10 reference images and only the documented size options.
Does not process images offline; prompts and image URLs are sent to RunComfy.

use_cases.title: Localize Campaign Images
use_cases.description: Replace in-image headlines with exact translated text while preserving the original layout, brand mark, and product framing.

use_cases.title: Create Brand-Safe Variants
use_cases.description: Change backgrounds, calls to action, or layout positions while keeping faces, products, and brand elements stable.

use_cases.title: Build Multi-Reference Composites
use_cases.description: Combine a subject from one image with the setting, lighting, or color palette from other reference images.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Background Edit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a single image edit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gpt-image-edit to keep the product unchanged and replace the background with a clean studio sweep. Use size auto.

prompt_templates.title: Localized Headline Swap
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for exact in-image text replacement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gpt-image-edit to replace only the headline with the exact translated text I provide. Preserve the photograph, logo, layout, and font weight.

prompt_templates.title: Two-Image Composition
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt using a primary image and one reference image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gpt-image-edit with two image URLs. Keep the subject from image 1 and match the room lighting and color palette from image 2.

prompt_templates.title: Production Edit Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for planning and quality checks before execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my source image URLs, desired edits, protected elements, and output size. Produce a preservation-first edit prompt, RunComfy execution plan, and checks for drift.

output_examples.input: A product photo needs a warmer studio background while the product shape and label stay unchanged.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a preservation-first edit prompt, recommends size auto, and prepares a RunComfy CLI workflow for the image URL.

output_examples.input: A poster headline must change from English to Japanese while the rest of the poster remains fixed.
output_examples.output: The skill quotes the exact replacement text, scopes the edit to the headline, and warns against changing the layout or brand mark.

output_examples.input: A subject from one image should appear inside a room from another image with matching light.
output_examples.output: The skill numbers each reference image, assigns subject and scene roles, and creates a prompt that preserves identity and matches lighting.

best_practices: Start each edit prompt with the faces, products, logos, layout, and framing that must remain unchanged.
Quote exact in-image text and name the writing system when replacing multilingual copy.
Use size auto unless the edit intentionally changes framing or aspect ratio.
anti_patterns: Combining many unrelated edits in one request, which increases visual drift.
Passing private image URLs without confirming they can be shared with RunComfy.
Paraphrasing replacement image text when the final copy must be exact.

faq.question: Does this skill edit images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the local RunComfy CLI to send requests to the RunComfy Model API.

faq.question: What inputs does it need?
faq.answer: It needs an edit prompt, one or more publicly fetchable HTTPS image URLs, and an optional size setting.

faq.question: How many reference images are supported?
faq.answer: The documented edit endpoint supports up to 10 image URLs, with the first image treated as primary.

faq.question: Can it replace text inside an image?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill gives prompt guidance for exact multilingual text replacement while preserving the rest of the image.

faq.question: Does it require credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. The RunComfy CLI requires login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN environment variable before requests can run.

faq.question: When should another model be used?
faq.answer: Use another model for larger batch workflows, strongest portrait photorealism, or source-fidelity-first local edits.
